host: Claude Agent SDK (Python) with Claude Code
covers: every tool call Claude Code reports to the PreToolUse hook of options wrapped by GroundedAgentAdapter.wrap_options(), including tools in allowed_tools
does_not_cover: a tool's own nested calls (an MCP tool calling another service); calls of a session whose options were not wrapped
scope: this adapter instance: every session and subagent it serves, ordered by its lock; a checkpoint it reads back from its checkpoint_dir, taken by an earlier process or by another adapter on that directory, authorises none of its calls; serve sessions that must not share records with separate adapters
boundaries: Stop of any session this adapter serves (its main agent's turn ends)
UserPromptSubmit of any session this adapter serves (a turn starts, which also ends what a turn left when its Stop never came)

Bash.mechanism: Claude Code's sandbox for Bash commands (Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux), turned on (enabled true) by the settings GroundedAgentAdapter.wrap_options() passes to the CLI's --settings: the options' sandbox, a strict one unless the host gives its own, and permissions.deny rules in their settings
Bash.routes_outside: allowUnsandboxedCommands is false, so the CLI ignores dangerouslyDisableSandbox, and the adapter gives a call that sets it the worst case; excludedCommands is empty; allowAllUnixSockets, allowLocalBinding, allowAppleEvents, allowNestedUserNamespaces, enableWeakerNestedSandbox and enableWeakerNetworkIsolation are false, allowUnixSockets and allowMachLookup are empty, and no proxy port of the host's own is set, so a sandboxed process reaches no local socket, loopback port, Mach service or application outside the sandbox but the sandbox's own network proxy
Bash.writes: The sandbox's write scope (the working directory and the sandbox's temporary directories; the adapter verifies that no directory is added to it; on macOS the temporary directory is Claude Code's own per-user directory, /tmp/claude-<uid>, which also holds other Claude Code sessions' temporary files, so a sandboxed command can change those, while nothing the adapter runs or reads as configuration lies there), less every path a permissions.deny Edit rule names, which the CLI applies to sandboxed commands and to the file tools: the adapter's records (checkpoint_dir, audit_log_path, the snapshot store, a file evidence store, and acs/ in the git directory and the common git directory), each also denied to Read; the plugin hooks' records, as grounded_agency/layer_records.py gives them (Edit of the project's .claude/checkpoint.ok, .claude/checkpoints/, .claude/audit.log and .claude/audit.head, and Edit and Read of acs/ in each git directory of the repository: the main checkout's, each linked worktree's and each submodule's, and, from a submodule checkout, each superproject's, as they exist when the options are wrapped); the project's .claude/ and .mcp.json; config, config.worktree and hooks in the git directory and the common git directory, and a linked worktree's .git file; the user's Claude Code settings, hooks, plugins, agents, commands and skills, and its .claude.json; and the code that runs outside the sandbox: the grounded_agency and claude_agent_sdk packages (with the CLI the SDK bundles), the interpreter, its site-packages directories and, where it lies in the project, its prefix, the CLI cli_path names, each local plugin, and, for each stdio MCP server of the options' mcp_servers and (unless strict_mcp_config) of the project's .mcp.json and the user's .claude.json, its command (and its path in each PATH directory inside the project) and every argument that names an existing file. Each path is literal and absolute, and where it is a link both the link and the path it resolves to are named, when the options are wrapped. The sandbox sets no allowWrite or allowRead, and filesystem.disabled is false. A record, a settings file, an MCP server list, a hook script, git configuration or a file a stdio server or the CLI runs that has a second hard link leaves the boundary unverified; the package, interpreter and plugin trees are protected by their deny rules alone, not walked for hard links
Bash.credentials: credentials.files deny entries, filesystem.denyRead entries and Read deny rules, under the CLI's home directory and this process's where they differ, for the macOS keychains (~/Library/Keychains, /Library/Keychains), ~/.ssh, ~/.gnupg, ~/.git-credentials, ~/.netrc, ~/.aws, ~/.azure, ~/.config/gcloud, ~/.kube, ~/.docker/config.json, ~/.npmrc, ~/.pypirc, ~/.cargo/credentials and credentials.toml, ~/.local/share/keyrings and ~/.password-store, gh's configuration directory, git's credentials file under XDG_CONFIG_HOME, the plugin's audit key file (~/.config/acs/audit.key), Claude Code's .credentials.json, and the paths GroundedAgentConfig.sandbox_deny_paths adds; credentials.envVars deny entries that unset GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, AUDIT_HMAC_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, SSH_AUTH_SOCK and GPG_AGENT_INFO, every variable of the CLI's environment whose name holds TOKEN, SECRET, PASSWORD, PASSWD, CREDENTIAL, API_KEY, ACCESS_KEY, PRIVATE_KEY, SESSION_KEY or AUTH, and those GroundedAgentConfig.sandbox_deny_env adds, for sandboxed commands. With the keychain files denied, the security command and git's credential helper find no item; with every Unix socket closed, the SSH and GPG agents are out of reach. A credential file with a second hard link, or a credential-like variable set in this process after the wrap that the sandbox does not unset, leaves the boundary unverified
Bash.network: network.allowedDomains is GroundedAgentConfig.sandbox_allowed_domains, empty by default (no host), with strictAllowlist true, under which the sandbox's proxy refuses a connection to any host not on it; a sandboxed command has no route to the network, name lookups included, but that proxy. An entry the plugin's setup command would not list (grounded_agency.sandbox_settings.check_host: anything but a dotted DNS name whose last label is alphabetic, with at most a leading *. wildcard; a loopback, link-local, metadata or local-use name such as one under .local; an IP literal in any spelling), any metadata. name, and an entry with a port or an IPv6 literal leave the boundary unverified, and so does a non-empty list while a destination policy is in force (allowed_destinations or a profile's), since a call read as local leaves send out
Bash.verification: When it wraps options, the adapter builds the --settings object as the Agent SDK does (the settings object with the options' sandbox as its sandbox member) and checks every value named above in it, autoAllowBashIfSandboxed false included (a caller's own sandbox must set it), that neither it nor allowed_tools holds a WebFetch allow rule or an Edit, Write or Read allow rule with a path (the CLI merges them into the sandbox), that it sets no permissions.additionalDirectories and no CLAUDE_CODE_SANDBOX variable in its env, that add_dirs is empty, that extra_args passes no flag but debug-to-stderr (the SDK passes extra_args after its own flags, so any other may override them), that mcp_servers is not given as a file or text, and that no path it denies holds a character a rule reads as a pattern. The home directory, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, XDG_CONFIG_HOME and GH_CONFIG_DIR are those of the CLI's environment (this process's with the options' env over it). It then reads the other settings sources the CLI reads: the managed settings files (managed-settings.json and managed-settings.d/ in the platform's directory) and the user's, the project's and the local settings file the options' setting_sources loads, and finds no sandbox value, allow rule, additionalDirectories entry or CLAUDE_CODE_SANDBOX variable in their env there that may weaken the boundary (any value of the list above, any allowedDomains entry included); a file there that cannot be read, a source it does not read that is present (a managed preferences profile on macOS, server-managed settings, the Windows policy registry), and a CLAUDE_CODE_SANDBOX variable in the environment leave the boundary unverified. Before it classifies each Bash call, it checks that none of those files changed since the options were wrapped, that the options it wrapped (their settings, sandbox, allowed_tools, extra_args, add_dirs, plugins, env, setting_sources, mcp_servers, cli_path and cwd) are unchanged while the caller holds them, and that no record, credential file or link-checked file named above has a second hard link. The boundary holds for a call only while every options the adapter wrapped hold it. failIfUnavailable is true, so the CLI refuses to start when it cannot apply the sandbox. A call whose dangerouslyDisableSandbox is set to anything but false gets the worst case. An unverified boundary gives every Bash call its worst case, not R407. The sources the CLI reads and the values it honours from each, which these checks rely on, are measured under Claude Code 2.1.332, the CLI claude-agent-sdk 0.2.189 bundles: on 2026-11-25 (RFC-0011), and on 2026-11-28 with the bundled CLI, each run reporting claude_code_version 2.1.332, by the Claude Code cases of tests/test_sandbox_boundary.py (22 passed with the settings given at start; with the settings at user scope, 5 passed and the 4 overrides from a file of higher precedence got through, as expected) and the adapter's live test (tests/test_sandbox_live.py: the bundled CLI, bypassPermissions mode, setting_sources empty; passed). A CLI that cli_path names, an SDK that bundles no CLI (it then runs the claude on PATH), and a bundled CLI of another version leave the boundary unverified (grounded_agency.utils.sandbox.CHECKED_CLI_VERSIONS). The boundary holds for a call only in the permission mode bypassPermissions (grounded_agency.utils.sandbox.CHECKED_PERMISSION_MODES), the one mode in which the precedence of settings files was tested; the routes the CLI decides itself (the escape argument, excluded commands, the network allowlist) were also tested in default and acceptEdits, but not which files can override them there. The PreToolUse hook reads the mode of each call from its hook input, else from the options, and a call that names neither runs in default; a call in any other mode gets the worst case, and options whose permission_mode, or a settings file read above whose permissions.defaultMode, is another mode leave the boundary unverified. In bypassPermissions no person is asked, so a call that requires approval is refused with F502 unless approval is off. The hook decides once for each call whether the boundary holds, and classifies the call and keeps it for after the call from that one decision. A Bash call is classified after it ran (the checkpoint it took, the capabilities that ran) only as the PreToolUse hook classified it: one it gave the worst case because the boundary did not hold then is the worst case afterwards too
outside: The adapter's hooks (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, Stop, UserPromptSubmit, SubagentStop), its can_use_tool callback and its checkpoint recorder, which run in the host's Python process
The git commands the adapter runs on its own behalf, with core.fsmonitor and hooks turned off
The tools create_grounded_mcp_server serves, in the host's Python process, and any MCP server the options, the project's .mcp.json or the user's .claude.json start
The hooks of a local plugin and of the user's and the project's settings
Claude Code's own file tools (Read, Edit, Write), which the deny rules and the adapter's checks govern

prompt_configurations: Claude Code permission mode default, acceptEdits or plan: the PreToolUse hook answers ask and can_use_tool decides, applying the binding's approval.expires from the ask; in any other mode the call is refused with F502

The same modes with a permission_prompt_tool_name, which decides a call that requires approval and no checkpoint, whose binding sets no approval.expires, of a tool create_grounded_mcp_server does not serve: the adapter never sees that tool's allow, so a call that requires a checkpoint is refused with R407 (no check again of its checkpoint when it is allowed), one whose binding sets approval.expires with F502 (no time of the decision), and one of a tool it serves with R407 (the tool runs only a call the adapter saw allowed)

concurrency_note: CheckpointTracker's lock makes a check, a hold and its use one atomic step; a hold is re-checked and used in one step when can_use_tool allows the call; adapters that share a checkpoint_dir write its state file under a file lock
host_gaps: The PreToolUse matcher sets on_failure "block", so a callback that fails or gives no verdict in time, as the CLI sees it, blocks the call, and the SDK refuses to connect to a Claude Code that does not honour it; a claude-agent-sdk whose HookMatcher has no on_failure cannot ask for it (the adapter logs a warning), and there such a callback is no decision and the call runs

The permission mode is read from the hook input, else from the wrapped options: a host that changes the mode during a session and omits it from hook input is checked against the mode the session started in
That Claude Code puts an ask to can_use_tool in modes default, acceptEdits and plan rests on its documentation; the tests call the hook and the callback directly
strict_mode=False, approval='off', check_outputs=False or create_grounded_mcp_server(require_layer=False) is outside class SL

A tool create_grounded_mcp_server serves runs a call only on this layer's decision, granted when the call is allowed (the PreToolUse hook's pass, or can_use_tool's allow of a call it asked about) and withdrawn by any refusal the adapter makes or when the call reports back; the SDK passes the tool's handler no call id, so the decision is matched by tool name and arguments: a caller outside the session that shares the server object and makes the same call between the allow and the call, or after a refusal the adapter never hears of (another PreToolUse hook's deny, an interrupt) of a call allowed without asking, before the next boundary, runs that allowed call in its place

§4.4.2 and §5.18.4, destination policies: the adapter does not see a tool's nested calls, so while a destination policy is in force it refuses with F504 every call of a composite whose invokes reach, transitively, a binding that performs send, wherever that send would go

Every PreToolUse hook is given the input the model wrote, and Claude Code then runs the call with another hook's updatedInput in its place: can_use_tool decides only on the input this layer's PreToolUse hook checked (another input is changed arguments, §5.18.7: F504, F501 or F502; a call the hook has no record of is R407), but a call the hook passed that Claude Code's own rules then allow without can_use_tool (allowed_tools, an allow rule, bypassPermissions) runs with the rewritten input, which this layer sees only at PostToolUse. The classifier relaxes Bash only in bypassPermissions, so every Bash call it relaxes is such a call. A host that adds a hook returning updatedInput keeps the tools it rewrites out of those rules, and does not run a hook that rewrites Bash calls in bypassPermissions
calls_without_output: §5.18.10 output-contract row, §5.20 hosts outside a workflow and §5.21.3's minimum confidence: the adapter receives a capability output from every MCP tool bound to a capability, whose result carries it as the I-JSON text of the output object, its one text content item (§5.18.9), and checks the text the session reads against the capability's output contract (R402), then GroundedAgentConfig.grounding and the applied profiles' grounding policies (F505) and their minimum confidence (F504): a tool create_grounded_mcp_server serves checks its own result (with require_layer; the SDK's server delivers a result's content and is_error, not its structuredContent), and the PostToolUse hook checks the result of any other, as Claude Code passes it, and replaces a refused result with the refusal (updatedMCPToolOutput). Claude Code's own tools (Read, Grep, Glob, WebFetch, Bash, ...) return results in their own forms, which carry no capability output, so no output check applies to their calls and their results are passed on as they are. The adapter logs a warning, once per tool, when a policy requires the capability of such a call or a profile sets a minimum confidence
